angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 9,447,606 km at 79.18 pc = 1.6 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 116076: distance 79.177 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.021), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 79.177 +/- 1.663 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 13.1681 +/- 0.0727 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94), 181.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 13.58 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 116076: radius 13.58 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 68.489 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.059) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 9,447,606 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4509 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 116076: effective temperature 4509 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.131) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 116076: effective temperature 4509 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.131) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 14 And (pscomppars): spectral type K0 III, from Teng et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023PASJ...75.1030T/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 14 And (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.21 dex, from Teng et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023PASJ...75.1030T/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 14 And (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 1.83992, from Teng et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023PASJ...75.1030T/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 14 And (pscomppars): age 4.5 Gyr, from Baines et al. 2009 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...701..154B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of 14 And (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.6 km/s, from Sato et al. 2008 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2008PASJ...60.1317S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.52 from 2024A&A...691A..53S; the 26 published values span log g 2.2 to 2.89, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...691A..53S)
